name: Keerak
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Robert & Segerer 2024, 'Joola Keeraak' (HAL hal-01513257, PDF behind bot-wall); also Sane 2005, 'Phonologie distributionelle du Her (parler diola de Kabrousse)', 110pp.

sources.citation: Robert, Stéphane & Guillaume Segerer. 2024. Joola Keeraak [: A grammatical introduction]. In Friederike Lüpke (ed.), The Oxford guide to the Atlantic languages of West Africa, 238-262. Oxford: Oxford University Press. DOI 10.1093/oso/9780198736516.003.0011. Author preprint (final v2, 55 pp.), HAL hal-01513257v2.
sources.note: Nothing. Section 2 'Phonology' (preprint pp. 3-6; §2.1 consonants, §2.2 vowels incl. 'Vowel length is phonemic', §2.3 phonotactics: consonant clusters, syllables, vowel harmony) never mentions stress, accent, tone, pitch, intonation or prosody; a full-text search of all 55 pages returns zero hits for stress/accent/tone/tonal/pitch/prosod/intonation/suprasegmental. Transcription note (p. 3) only says examples use an IPA-based phonological transcription with long vowels written double.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page kera1248 and reference pages 40104, 65308; LLACAN page of Guillaume Segerer (https://llacan.cnrs.fr/p_segerer.php).
sources.note: Bibliographic only. Segerer's page lists no Keerak phonology publication and no downloadable Keerak PDFs; Glottolog lists exactly three descriptive refs (Sane 2005, Robert & Segerer 2020/2024, Segerer 2015).
